concept.logline: One bakery's fire changed what London was made of, and how many it killed is still unknown.
concept.viewer_change: They know the fire's size and ending, accept that the death toll is uncertain, and connect the rebuilding to the fire.
concept.central_metaphor: a city assembled from paper, burned away, and rebuilt in a different material

arc.notes: consequence is used twice: the measurable loss (s3) and the unmeasurable one (s4). Library stage 'resolution' closes.

global_direction.sound_design: warm low bed; paper, stamp and brick foley sit 12-18 dB under the voice; silence before the loss figure and before the ending; no whooshes on scene changes
global_direction.pacing: a new picture every 2-3 s except the declared breath in s4

beats.purpose: Place the viewer at the exact origin in time and place: one bakery, just after midnight.
beats.viewer_takeaway: The fire began small, in one ordinary building.
beats.narration: A little after midnight on Sunday the second of September, sixteen sixty-six, a fire broke out in a baker's shop on Pudding Lane.
beats.visual_concept: A torn map sheet slides onto kraft paper; a taped banner names the lane; a paper flame is pinned to one spot and flickers beside a tiny bakery cut-out.

shots.composition: map sheet left-centre, banner top-right, flame pinned low-centre
shots.typography: Archivo Black banner, Space Mono date tape

audio.intent: room-tone, one soft paper slide, a pin tap

assets.reason: paper grain is texture, code makes it well and reproducibly
flat cut-out shapes are exact in SVG; generation would add nothing

beats.purpose: Show duration and how it ended: four days, ended when the wind dropped and firebreaks held.
beats.viewer_takeaway: It lasted four days and was stopped by wind and firebreaks, not by putting it out.
beats.narration: It burned until Wednesday. Only when the wind dropped and firebreaks took hold was the fire finally over.
beats.visual_concept: Four day tickets are stamped down one by one as a torn burn-shape spreads across a schematic city and turns to charcoal when the wind note is taped on.

shots.composition: day tickets in a row across the top, burn shape lower-left spreading right
shots.object_movement: stamp thud, burn grows stepwise, smoke scraps rise

transition_in.motivation: the next paper sheet is pushed over the last: time moves on

audio.intent: stamp thuds on each day, a low crackle bed that fades when the wind drops

assets.reason: schematic by design: no claim about the real burn extent

beats.purpose: State the scale of the loss with the sources' own ranges.
beats.viewer_takeaway: Thousands of homes and dozens of churches, including the cathedral, were lost.
beats.narration: By then, an estimated thirteen thousand houses, about eighty-seven parish churches, and Saint Paul's Cathedral had been destroyed.
beats.visual_concept: A huge counter on a torn vermilion sheet rolls to 13,200 while a row of paper houses chars one by one, then a row of churches and a dome fall to charcoal and are stamped RUIN.

shots.composition: counter sheet left, house row beneath, church row and dome right
shots.typography: Archivo Black numeral, mono range caption

transition_in.motivation: a torn-edge wipe: the sheet is ripped away to reveal what was lost

audio.intent: low rising tone under the counter, silence just before the stamp

beats.purpose: Be honest that the human cost is uncertain, and give that uncertainty room.
key_information: disputed; some historians argue far higher
beats.viewer_takeaway: The number that is usually quoted may be far too low, and nobody can be sure.
beats.narration: The death toll is still debated. The traditional figure is just six, but some historians think it was far higher.
beats.visual_concept: Almost empty kraft: one typed line, a single paper '6' in a circle, and a lightly ghosted question mark that grows behind it.

shots.composition: line upper-left third, circle sticker right of centre, lots of paper
shots.typography: Space Mono line, Archivo Black numeral

transition_in.motivation: calm: the loud sheet fades from one object, not a scene wipe

audio.intent: bed thins to almost nothing; no foley; one soft typewriter tick per word cluster

assets.reason: same plate as s1: continuity and no extra generation

beats.purpose: Show what changed: a different city, built in brick and stone, with the Monument as memory.
key_information: Rebuilding of London Act 1666: no wooden exteriors
beats.viewer_takeaway: The fire changed what London was made of.
beats.narration: London was rebuilt in brick and stone, not wood. Christopher Wren rebuilt Saint Paul's, and the Monument, two hundred and two feet tall, still marks the fire.
beats.visual_concept: The circle sticker becomes the dome of St Paul's; bricks stack into a skyline replacing timber houses, WOOD is struck out, and a paper column grows to a 202 ft tape-measure label. It ends smaller than it began.

shots.composition: skyline across the lower half, dome left, Monument column right, title small centre
shots.typography: Archivo Black struck word, mono height label

transition_in.motivation: the paper '6' circle carries over and becomes the dome: the calm circle turns into the rebuilt city

audio.intent: bed warms and rises slightly; brick placements as soft thocks; final 1.4 s near-silent
